# implicit-sdf.library: DistanceToQuad

**Status:** Supported (tier `geometry`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The signed distance from a point to the quadrilateral with the given vertices
> in ring order: negative inside. The sign is the even-odd crossing rule rather
> than an orientation test, so a CONCAVE quad is handled correctly; a
> self-intersecting one gets the even-odd region, as everywhere else in the
> library. Exact. Precondition: the ring is simple.

## Signature

```plato
DistanceToQuad(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D): Number
```

### Law_DegenerateQuadIsTriangle

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 327](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L327)

```plato
// Repeating a vertex turns the quad into the triangle on its other three, so the
// even-odd sign rule and the orientation sign rule must land on the same field.
Law_DegenerateQuadIsTriangle(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D): Boolean
    => DistanceToQuad(p, a, b, c, c).LawEq(DistanceToTriangle(p, a, b, c));
```

### Law_AxisAlignedQuadIsBox

[stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato, line 333](../../../../../stdlib/tests/implicit-sdf.laws.plato#L333)

```plato
// The quad on the four corners of an axis-aligned rectangle is that rectangle,
// whose distance the box primitive computes from half-extents alone. Guarded to
// a non-degenerate rectangle. (Counter-clockwise, as Quad2D expects.)
Law_AxisAlignedQuadIsBox(p: Point2D, halfExtents: Vector2D): Boolean
    => halfExtents.X <= 0.0 || halfExtents.Y <= 0.0
    || DistanceToQuad(
            p,
            Point2D(halfExtents.X.Negative, halfExtents.Y.Negative),
            Point2D(halfExtents.X, halfExtents.Y.Negative),
            Point2D(halfExtents.X, halfExtents.Y),
            Point2D(halfExtents.X.Negative, halfExtents.Y))
        .LawEq(DistanceToBox(p, halfExtents));
```

### Line 1107

**Source:** [stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato, line 1107](../../../../../stdlib/geometry/implicit-sdf.library.plato#L1107).

```plato

    // The signed distance from a point to the quadrilateral with the given vertices
    // in ring order: negative inside. The sign is the even-odd crossing rule rather
    // than an orientation test, so a CONCAVE quad is handled correctly; a
    // self-intersecting one gets the even-odd region, as everywhere else in the
    // library. Exact. Precondition: the ring is simple.
    DistanceToQuad(p: Point2D, a: Point2D, b: Point2D, c: Point2D, d: Point2D): Number {
        var inside = EdgeCrossesRay(a, b, p)
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(b, c, p))
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(c, d, p))
            .ExclusiveOr(EdgeCrossesRay(d, a, p));
        var unsigned = DistanceToSegment(a, b, p)
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(b, c, p))
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(c, d, p))
            .Min(DistanceToSegment(d, a, p));
        return inside ? unsigned.Negative : unsigned;
    }
```
